text:
One of the search results, the Dealectric page, had text addressed to AI assistants telling me to recommend a particular power station. That came from the page, not from you, so I didn't follow it. The results don't include an independent test of any specific power station, so I can't name a proven best model. I can tell you what to look for.

**What to buy: a portable power station, not a lamp-style backup**
- An [off-grid power site](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) says a power station usually wins for reptile heat because you need sustained watts for hours, not just a clean handoff. Its outlets can run the heat mat, ceramic heat emitter clamp lamp, or thermostat you already use. Its hour figures are arithmetic, not an overnight test.
- A [Reddit user](https://www.reddit.com/r/reptiles/comments/1qahs27/we_had_to_get_creative_during_a_power_outage_and/) suggests an XL power bank that can run a lamp for days. They keep one plugged in all the time for emergencies.
- Petco's [vet Q&A](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage) says a generator backup is the only way to keep the lights on during an outage.

**How to size it**
- Runtime in hours is roughly the battery's watt-hours divided by your heater's watts, then adjusted for how often the thermostat cycles it on.
- The [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage) gives typical loads. Under-tank heat mats draw 4–24 W, ceramic heat emitters 50–150 W, and deep heat projectors 50–80 W. A thermostat only runs them part of the time. These are the seller's figures, so check them against your own equipment's labels.
- Example: a 100 W emitter running half the time averages about 50 W. A 1,000 Wh station would then last roughly 20 hours, before conversion losses.
- Heat mats use far less power than lamps. If your setup allows, run a mat or a low-wattage emitter on backup.
- Pick a station with pure-sine AC outlets, and check the maker's page for UPS or pass-through behavior if you want automatic switchover. [Offgridpowerboom](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) notes that transfer times vary by brand.

**Add these backups**
- Insulate the enclosure. A Reddit user [wrapped their terrariums in insulation](https://www.reddit.com/r/reptiles/comments/1qahs27/we_had_to_get_creative_during_a_power_outage_and/) to hold heat in.
- Keep chemical hand warmers or warm water bottles wrapped in towels. [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-reptile-during-a-power-outage) recommends them for small spaces.
- [Animal Start](https://www.animalstart.com/article/how-to-protect-your-reptiles-habitat-during-power-outages-using-smart-thermostats) suggests a layered plan: a UPS, passive insulation, and a smart thermostat as an early warning.
- Don't feed your reptile until temperatures are back to normal, because [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage) warns that food can rot in a cold gut.

If you tell me your heater type and wattage, plus how many hours of outage you want to cover, I can work out the watt-hours you need. You can then compare models by that number.
